# The cell-type classifier's arity bug — diagnosis, fix, three-section audit

*Generated by `./.venv/bin/python -m tmesim.validation.classifier_fix`. Every number below is recomputed from the cached real bytes at run time.*

## 0. Verdict first

| ENDOTHELIAL % of cells | s1 | s2 | s3 | spread (max/min) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **before** (`mean_z`, the bug) | 9.74 | 4.18 | 12.19 | **2.91x** |
| **after** (`matched_null_z`) | 10.50 | 7.07 | 8.75 | **1.49x** |

Consistency improved: the endothelial fraction's cross-section spread fell from **2.91x** to **1.49x** (CV 47% -> 20%). It did NOT collapse to a single value, and the report says so plainly in §6. The target was consistency, not the 8.0% volume-EM anchor, which was never optimised against — the gate stayed fixed at 1.0 for every candidate.

## 1. The bug, measured

`phenotype_cells` scored a type by the MEAN z-score of its markers and gated that score at a fixed 1.0. Each marker z-score has unit variance by construction, so the mean of `n` of them has standard deviation

```
    sd(mean-z) = sqrt( (1 + (n-1) * rho) / n )        rho = mean pairwise marker correlation
```

which shrinks with `n`. A **fixed** gate on a score whose spread depends on the marker count is therefore easier to clear the fewer markers a type has. This is arithmetic, not biology, and the measured spread matches the closed form to three decimals on every section:

**s1 — Xenium Human Brain 319-gene GBM (10x preview)** · 40,887 cells · 319 panel genes · marker map `brain_319`

Read the `sd(mean-z)` and `% clearing gate (mean_z)` columns together. On s1 and s3 the one-marker `ENDOTHELIAL` class has sd exactly 1.000 while every multi-marker class sits at 0.55-0.87, and endothelium is correspondingly the most permissive gate of the four (11.76% on s1 against 7.29-10.94%; 14.03% on s3 against 5.92-6.58%, i.e. 2.1-2.4x the next class). On s2, where the panel forces a THREE-marker endothelial gate (VWF/FLT1/PLVAP), the sd drops to 0.821 and the clearing rate collapses to 4.57% — now the LOWEST of the four. **The class did not change; the number of genes defining it did.**

The `max_z` column is the counter-demonstration. Where endothelium has one marker it clears at 11.76% (s1) and 14.03% (s3) against 23-38% for the 3- and 4-marker classes — the arity bias with its sign flipped, exactly as `E[max of n]` growing with `n` predicts. `matched_null_z` is the only rule whose clearing rates are not ordered by marker count on any section.

The same point in terms of score SPREAD (the SD of each type's score across cells, which is what a fixed gate cuts into):

| section | type | n | sd(`mean_z`) | sd(`max_z`) | sd(`matched_null_z`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| s1 | TUMOR | 4 | 0.607 | 1.343 | 1.298 |
| s1 | STROMAL | 3 | 0.675 | 0.865 | 1.061 |
| s1 | IMMUNE | 4 | 0.780 | 1.190 | 1.548 |
| s1 | ENDOTHELIAL | 1 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.417 |
| s2 | TUMOR | 4 | 0.554 | 1.346 | 1.242 |
| s2 | STROMAL | 3 | 0.865 | 0.814 | 1.179 |
| s2 | IMMUNE | 4 | 0.705 | 1.514 | 1.136 |
| s2 | ENDOTHELIAL | 3 | 0.821 | 1.401 | 1.915 |
| s3 | TUMOR | 4 | 0.637 | 0.992 | 1.107 |
| s3 | STROMAL | 3 | 0.664 | 1.208 | 1.366 |
| s3 | IMMUNE | 4 | 0.681 | 1.493 | 1.240 |
| s3 | ENDOTHELIAL | 1 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.348 |

Under `mean_z` the spread is a deterministic function of `n` and the 1-marker class is *always* the widest. Under `matched_null_z` the spread tracks how much real signal a marker set carries, and the 1-marker class is no longer systematically the widest — which is the property the fix is supposed to have.

Two things this rules out. It is not purely a panel artefact: s1 and s3 use the identical PECAM1 gate and still differ 1.25x, because the arity bias interacts with each section's own marker detection rates (PECAM1 is seen in 24.6% of s1 cells and 14.0% of s3 cells). And it is not the marker map being wrong: the same map, scored differently, gives a consistent answer (§3).

## 2. Candidate aggregations

Five rules, all gated at the **same fixed** `TYPING_THRESHOLD = 1.0`, so the comparison isolates the aggregation and nothing is tuned.

| rule | what the score is | controls arity? | controls detection rate / depth? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mean_z` | mean marker z (LEGACY) | no — this is the bug | no |
| `max_z` | largest single marker z | no — biased the *other* way, `E[max of n]` grows with `n` | no |
| `marker_vote` | fraction of markers individually z>=1, max-z tie-break, >=1 required | no — a 1-marker type saturates the score at 1.0 | partially (per-marker call) |
| `mean_z_norm` | mean-z / its own SD across cells (the `1/sqrt(n)` variance correction) | **yes** | no |
| `matched_null_z` | per-cell z of the mean-z against a same-size, detection-rate-matched RANDOM gene set | **yes** | **yes** |

`matched_null_z` is option (c) of the brief and is the same control the MGMT spatial work used (`validation/mgmt_spatial.py`, abundance-matched reference genes). For each marker it takes the 25 panel genes closest in logit-detection-rate (markers of any type excluded), and computes the null mean and variance of the same-size random signature **analytically over the pool** — `E[score] = (1/n) sum_s mean_pool z`, `Var[score] = (1/n^2) sum_s var_pool z` — so the null is exact, deterministic and RNG-free. The gate then reads "this cell's marker-set signal is >= 1 SD above a size- and abundance-matched random signature", which is a statement of the same strength for a 1-marker and a 4-marker type.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `matched_null_z` | 10.50 | 7.07 | 8.75 | 8.77 | **1.49x** | 20% | 0.77 pp | 1.00 pp |

**Why `max_z` was NOT chosen despite the tightest endothelial spread.** Its tightness here is cancellation, not control: `E[max of n]` *grows* with `n`, so `max_z` is arity-biased in the opposite direction to `mean_z`, and on these particular panels (1-marker endothelium on two sections, 3-marker on the third) the two biases happen to partly offset. Change the marker count of any class and the cancellation disappears. It is also the least robust rule available — it types every cell off its single most extreme transcript count, so one spurious count reassigns a cell — and it moves the whole composition hardest (TUMOR 49-59%, IMMUNE 20-24%). Picking it would be selecting on the outcome we are trying to measure. `marker_vote` (option (a)) is rejected for the same reason in reverse: "fraction of markers positive" saturates at 1.0 for a one-marker type, so it *is* the arity bug wearing different clothes, and it inflates STROMAL to 19-30%.

`mean_z_norm` (option (b)) is the honest partial fix: it removes the arity term exactly, and the endothelial spread does fall 2.91x -> 2.01x. But it leaves the per-marker sparsity and per-cell depth confounds untouched, which is why s2 (whose endothelial markers are detected in 4-9% of cells vs PECAM1's 14-25%) is still the outlier. Only `matched_null_z` controls all three.

## 4. Anchor-free sanity check: are the labels still spatially real?

Nearest-neighbour label enrichment (k=10): the probability a cell's neighbour shares its type, divided by that type's global frequency. 1.0 = randomly scattered. Vessels, TAM nests and white-matter tracts are contiguous, so real compartments should sit well above 1.

| section | rule | TUMOR | STROMAL | IMMUNE | ENDOTHELIAL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| s1 | `mean_z` | 1.03 | 1.76 | 1.60 | 1.73 |
| s1 | `max_z` | 1.09 | 1.25 | 1.27 | 2.10 |
| s1 | `marker_vote` | 1.14 | 1.22 | 1.32 | 1.69 |
| s1 | `mean_z_norm` | 1.04 | 1.72 | 1.50 | 1.86 |
| s1 | `matched_null_z` | 1.08 | 1.63 | 1.51 | 1.81 |
| s2 | `mean_z` | 1.04 | 1.61 | 2.52 | 6.73 |
| s2 | `max_z` | 1.10 | 1.42 | 1.58 | 3.12 |
| s2 | `marker_vote` | 1.14 | 1.26 | 1.79 | 3.44 |
| s2 | `mean_z_norm` | 1.05 | 1.55 | 2.43 | 4.92 |
| s2 | `matched_null_z` | 1.05 | 1.58 | 1.83 | 3.28 |
| s3 | `mean_z` | 1.04 | 1.74 | 1.93 | 1.84 |
| s3 | `max_z` | 1.07 | 1.40 | 1.34 | 2.30 |
| s3 | `marker_vote` | 1.07 | 1.37 | 1.63 | 1.74 |
| s3 | `mean_z_norm` | 1.05 | 1.51 | 1.75 | 1.97 |
| s3 | `matched_null_z` | 1.05 | 1.41 | 1.41 | 2.16 |

**This is a guard, not a ranking statistic** — enrichment rises mechanically as a class shrinks toward its most-confident core, which is exactly why `mean_z` scores 6.73 on s2 while calling only 4.18% of cells endothelial. The point is the negative one: `matched_null_z` keeps endothelium at 1.8-3.3x above random on all three sections, so the extra cells it admits are spatially clustered with the ones the old rule already found, not scattered noise.

## 5. Cross-check against the independent Visium NNLS deconvolution

`reconstruct/deconvolve.py` on the real `10x_parent_gbm` Visium sample (3,468 spots): non-negative least squares of each spot against mean single-cell signatures from the Darmanis GBM atlas (GSE84465). **It uses no marker gate, no z-score and no threshold**, so it is genuinely independent of everything above.

| | TUMOR | STROMAL | IMMUNE | ENDOTHELIAL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Visium NNLS (independent) | **82.66%** | **1.04%** | **6.53%** | **9.77%** |
| classifier `mean_z`, mean of 3 sections | 76.52% | 7.90% | 6.87% | 8.71% |
| classifier `matched_null_z`, mean of 3 sections | 61.67% | 15.06% | 14.49% | 8.77% |

On ENDOTHELIAL — the only column the two methods can be sharply compared on — the independent estimate is **9.77%**. Per-section absolute distance to it:

| rule | s1 | s2 | s3 | mean | worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mean_z` (old) | 0.03 pp | 5.59 pp | 2.42 pp | **2.68 pp** | 5.59 pp |
| `matched_null_z` (new) | 0.73 pp | 2.70 pp | 1.02 pp | **1.49 pp** | 2.70 pp |

**The fixed classifier agrees BETTER with the independent NNLS estimate** (mean distance 2.68 pp -> 1.49 pp, worst-case 5.59 pp -> 2.70 pp).

**Three caveats, stated because this is the strongest-looking result here.** (i) The Visium sample is a DIFFERENT specimen from all three Xenium sections, so exact agreement would be luck; only the order of magnitude and the direction of the correction are meaningful. (ii) NNLS against a dissociation-based scRNA-seq reference has its own well-known biases — the same Darmanis-based deconvolution puts STROMAL at 1.04%, which is not credible for brain tissue and shows the method is not a gold standard, just an independent one. (iii) The agreement was not optimised for: the gate was frozen at 1.0 across all five candidates before any of these numbers were computed.

## 6. Honest verdict: is the fraction consistent now?

**Improved, materially, but NOT resolved.** The endothelial fraction still varies 1.49x across the three sections (10.50% / 7.07% / 8.75%), down from 2.91x (9.74% / 4.18% / 12.19%). The direction of the old error is also gone: the section that read *lowest* (s2, 4.18%) and the section that read *highest* (s3, 12.19%) have both moved toward the middle, which is what a genuine bias correction looks like and what a re-tuning would not have produced simultaneously.

What is fixed:

* The **marker count no longer biases assignment.** A 1-marker and a 4-marker type are now scored against equally-sized null signatures, so the gate means the same thing for both. This was the specific defect, and it is gone by construction, not by tuning.
* **Per-marker sparsity no longer biases assignment.** The null is matched on detection rate, so a gate built from 4%-detected markers (s2's VWF/PLVAP) is no longer harder to clear than one built from 25%-detected PECAM1.
* The three sections' **whole compositions** are far closer than they were: worst-type spread across the four classes falls from 2.91x to 1.71x.

What is NOT fixed, and why the residual spread should not be read as biology either:

1. **The residual is still partly measurement.** s2 is a different patient on a panel sharing only 60 genes with the other two; its endothelial class is built from entirely different genes (VWF/FLT1/PLVAP vs PECAM1). Matching on detection rate controls the *sparsity* of those genes, not their *specificity* — PLVAP is induced in GBM neovasculature and VWF is not uniformly expressed along a vessel, so the three-gene programme genuinely labels a different set of cells than PECAM1 does. No aggregation rule can fix a marker-set difference.
2. **Cell density differs 6x between sections**, so the *fraction* (an endothelial count divided by a total-cell count) is partly a statement about the denominator. Endothelial cells per mm² still differs far more across sections than the fraction does; see the last column of §3.
3. **Three sections is not a distribution.** A 1.5x spread on n=3 supports "the gross bias is gone", not "the classifier is calibrated". Nothing here licenses quoting a single endothelial fraction as a validated property of the method.
4. **The 8.0% volume-EM number remains an anchor, not a validation.** It is cortex, not tumour; it was never fitted to; and the fact that the corrected three-section mean (8.77%) lands near it is a consistency observation, not evidence the classifier is right. The previous claim that the 9.74% figure 'replicated volume EM' should be retired: that number was produced by the biased rule and its agreement was coincidental.
5. **A second-order residual in the fix itself, in the opposite direction.** The matched null draws its `n` reference genes INDEPENDENTLY, but a real marker set is a co-expressed programme (measured mean pairwise correlation: TUMOR 0.16, STROMAL 0.18, IMMUNE 0.48 on s1). Correlated markers make the observed score more variable than an independent null predicts, so the null SD is slightly too small for a coherent multi-marker programme and its z is nudged UP. That is part of why IMMUNE and STROMAL grow under the new rule. It is opposite in sign to the bug being fixed, it is second-order next to it (the original effect was a factor of `sqrt(n)`), and it is NOT corrected here — correcting it needs a null that reproduces the marker set's covariance, which cannot be built from detection-rate matching alone. Anyone reading a multi-marker class fraction off this classifier should treat it as a mild over-estimate.
6. **Every other class moved too.** TUMOR falls from 76.5% to 61.7% on average, because the matched null admits more positively-called cells overall and TUMOR is the ungated default. That is a real change to the reconstruction's composition and any downstream absolute number computed before this fix is conditional on the old, biased labels. The tumour fraction is still the majority class on all three sections, as a GBM resection requires.

## 7. What changed in the code

* `reconstruct/real_xenium.py` — `phenotype_cells` gains an `aggregation` argument (default `'matched_null_z'`) plus the matched-null machinery (`detection_rates`, `_matched_pool`, `_matched_null_moments`). `aggregation='mean_z'` reproduces the legacy labels bit-for-bit, so every historical number stays regenerable. `reconstruct_from_xenium` forwards the choice and records it in `metadata['typing_aggregation']`.
* `reconstruct/real_xenium.py` — `marker_scores` is split out of `phenotype_cells` so this audit and the tests read the SAME score arrays the classifier gates, and cannot drift from it.
* `validation/state_validation.py` — `check_brain_panel_unchanged` is the guard that proves the IO marker map is inert on the brain panel. It now checks that property under `aggregation='mean_z'` (the rule in force when its reference numbers were frozen) and REPORTS the current default alongside, instead of failing on a change of default it was never about.
* `reconstruct/marker_panels.py` — docstring only: the 73.80/7.92/8.54/9.74 numbers are relabelled as the legacy-scoring composition, and the IO map's claim that three endothelial markers 'removes the single-vs-multi-marker imbalance' is corrected — it reversed the imbalance's sign.
* Nothing in `core/`, `physics/` or `sim/engine.py` was touched. No drug, PK or response-validation code was touched.
* `tests/test_classifier_arity.py` pins the fixed behaviour on section 1 and pins the arity relationship itself (`sd(mean-z)` vs the closed form) so the bug cannot silently return.
